reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / ACR-EULAR
clinicalPearls: An inflammatory arthritis associated with psoriasis; skin disease usually precedes joint involvement but arthritis can appear first or without evident skin lesions

Presents in several patterns including asymmetric oligoarthritis, symmetric polyarthritis resembling rheumatoid arthritis, distal interphalangeal predominant disease, spondylitis, and the destructive arthritis mutilans
Dactylitis ('sausage digit') and enthesitis are hallmark features that help distinguish it from rheumatoid arthritis
Nail changes such as pitting and onycholysis correlate with distal interphalangeal joint involvement
Usually seronegative for rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibodies
Radiographs may show combined erosion and new bone formation, with the classic 'pencil-in-cup' deformity in advanced disease
Associated comorbidities include uveitis, inflammatory bowel disease, and increased cardiovascular and metabolic risk

Treatment is guided by domains involved (peripheral joints, axial disease, enthesitis, dactylitis, skin, nails), using NSAIDs, conventional DMARDs, and biologic or targeted synthetic agents (TNF, IL-17, IL-23, JAK inhibitors)
reference.pathophysiology: Psoriatic arthritis is a seronegative spondyloarthropathy resulting from immune-mediated inflammation in genetically predisposed individuals. Dysregulation of the TNF and IL-23/IL-17 axes drives inflammation at synovium, entheses, and skin. Unlike rheumatoid arthritis, both bone erosion and pathological new bone formation occur, producing the mixed destructive and proliferative changes seen radiographically. Enthesitis is considered a primary lesion, and there are associations with HLA-B27 (particularly axial disease) and other HLA alleles.
additionalDifferentials: Osteoarthritis, particularly of distal interphalangeal joints
additionalInvestigations: Examination of skin and nails for psoriasis, pitting, and onycholysis
Rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibodies to help distinguish from rheumatoid arthritis
Radiographs of hands, feet, and axial skeleton for erosions, new bone, and pencil-in-cup change
Ultrasound or MRI to detect enthesitis, synovitis, and dactylitis
Inflammatory markers and metabolic/cardiovascular risk screening
redFlags: Rapidly progressive, deforming or mutilating arthritis with joint destruction (arthritis mutilans)
Acute painful red eye indicating uveitis requiring ophthalmology review
Features suggesting axial disease with neurological compromise
Symptoms of undiagnosed inflammatory bowel disease
Extensive or erythrodermic/pustular skin disease indicating severe systemic involvement
reference.prognosis: Course ranges from mild intermittent arthritis to progressive erosive disease with joint destruction and disability. Early recognition and treat-to-target therapy improve outcomes; poor prognostic markers include polyarticular involvement, elevated inflammatory markers, early erosions, and dactylitis.
pitfalls: Missing the diagnosis when arthritis precedes or occurs without obvious skin psoriasis
Mislabelling it as rheumatoid arthritis and overlooking dactylitis, enthesitis, and nail disease
Failing to assess and treat all involved domains rather than joints alone
Neglecting cardiovascular, metabolic, and uveitis comorbidities
Assuming seronegativity excludes an inflammatory arthritis
management: NSAIDs and local corticosteroid injections for symptom relief in mild peripheral or entheseal disease
Conventional synthetic DMARDs such as methotrexate, leflunomide or sulfasalazine for persistent peripheral arthritis

Biologic therapy targeting tumour necrosis factor, interleukin-17 or interleukin-23, or targeted synthetic agents such as JAK inhibitors or apremilast, for inadequate response or predominant axial and entheseal disease
Adopt a treat-to-target approach aiming for minimal disease activity, with regular assessment of joints, entheses, dactylitis and skin
Physiotherapy, occupational therapy and exercise to preserve joint function, with orthopaedic referral for arthritis mutilans
Coordinate skin and joint care with dermatology and manage cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidity
Baseline and monitoring investigations with infection screening, including tuberculosis, before immunomodulatory therapy
